title: A smooth algebra over a field is a local complete intersection
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]: there are $g_i\in S$ ($i\in J$) with $\operatorname{Spec}S=\bigcup_iD(g_i)$ such that each localization $S_{g_i}$ is a global complete intersection over $k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00T5 (label lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180) and its proof (reduction to k algebraically closed by Lemmas 00T4 lemma-base-change-smooth and lemma-lci-field-change; Nullstellensatz; Nakayama; regular sequence by lemma-regular-ring-CM; condition (5) of Lemma 00SC lemma-lci at every maximal ideal)

proof.text: (Reduction to $k$ algebraically closed.) By [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] (i) $S$ is a finitely presented, in particular finite type, $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\iota:k\to\bar k$ be an algebraic closure of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] (it exists). By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (1) with $R=k$, $R'=\bar k$, the $\bar k$-algebra $\bar k\otimes_kS$ is smooth over $\bar k$; the swap $\bar k\otimes_kS\cong S\otimes_k\bar k$, $\lambda\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes\lambda$, is an isomorphism of $\bar k$-algebras, and smoothness [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] is invariant under isomorphism of $\bar k$-algebras (the three conditions are), so $S\otimes_k\bar k$ is a smooth $\bar k$-algebra. Suppose the lemma is proved for algebraically closed fields (steps 2-10, applied to $\bar k$ and $S\otimes_k\bar k$). Then $S\otimes_k\bar k$ is a local complete intersection over $\bar k$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-lci-field-change] (direction 'if', with $K=\bar k$; $S$ is of finite type) $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. From now on $k$ is algebraically closed.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180), first sentence: 'By Lemmas 00T4 (lemma-base-change-smooth) and 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change) it suffices to prove this when k is algebraically closed'

proof.text: (A presentation, and $\mathrm d$ is a split injection.) By [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] (i) there are $n,m\ge0$, $g_1,\dots,g_m\in P:=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and an isomorphism of $k$-algebras $P/(g_1,\dots,g_m)\cong S$; let $\alpha:P\to S$ be the composite surjection and $I=\ker\alpha=(g_1,\dots,g_m)$, a finitely generated ideal. Identify $S$ with $A:=P/I$ through $\alpha$; then $A$ is a smooth $k$-algebra. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-localization-conormal-split] with $R=k$, this $P$, $I$, $A$, and $a=1$: the localization $A_1$ at $\{1\}$ is $A$ itself ($a/1\mapsto a$ is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras [def-weil-ring-localization-away]), hence smooth, and $(I/I^2)_1=I/I^2$, so part (1) of that lemma says that the $S$-linear map $\mathrm d:I/I^2\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^nS\,\mathrm dx_i$, $\mathrm d(f\bmod I^2)=\sum_i\alpha(\partial f/\partial x_i)\,\mathrm dx_i$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative], has an $S$-linear left inverse $\lambda$: $\lambda\circ\mathrm d=\mathrm{id}_{I/I^2}$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180): 'Choose a presentation alpha: k[x_1..x_n] -> S with kernel I ... By our assumption that k -> S is smooth the S-module map d: I/I^2 -> (+) S dx_i is a split injection'

proof.text: (A maximal ideal and the Nullstellensatz.) Let $\mathfrak m\subset S$ be a maximal ideal and $\mathfrak m'=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$; then $I\subseteq\mathfrak m'$ and $P/\mathfrak m'\cong S/\mathfrak m=:\kappa$ is a field, so $\mathfrak m'$ is maximal. The field $\kappa$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra (generated by the classes of $x_1,\dots,x_n$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] it is a finite field extension of $k$, and as $k$ is algebraically closed, [lem-weil-pbc-alg-closed-finite-extension-trivial] shows that $k\to\kappa$ is bijective. Hence for each $i$ there is $a_i\in k$ with $x_i\equiv a_i\bmod\mathfrak m'$, i.e. $x_i-a_i\in\mathfrak m'$. Let $\mathrm{ev}_a:P\to k$ be the $k$-algebra map with $x_i\mapsto a_i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $\mathfrak n=(x_1-a_1,\dots,x_n-a_n)$. Every $p\in P$ satisfies $p\equiv\mathrm{ev}_a(p)\bmod\mathfrak n$ (true for $x_i$ and constants, and the set of such $p$ is closed under sums and products), so $\ker\mathrm{ev}_a=\mathfrak n$ and $P/\mathfrak n\cong k$; thus $\mathfrak n$ is maximal, and $\mathfrak n\subseteq\mathfrak m'\neq P$ gives $\mathfrak m'=\mathfrak n=(x_1-a_1,\dots,x_n-a_n)$. In particular every $p\in P$ satisfies $p\equiv p(a)\bmod\mathfrak m'$ with $p(a):=\mathrm{ev}_a(p)$, and $p(a)=0$ for $p\in\mathfrak m'$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180): 'We may write m' = (x_1 - a_1, ..., x_n - a_n) for some a_i in k, because k is algebraically closed, see Theorem 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz)'

proof.text: (The local ring $R=P_{\mathfrak m'}$.) Let $\tau:P\to P$ be the $k$-algebra map with $x_i\mapsto x_i+a_i$ and $\tau'$ the one with $x_i\mapsto x_i-a_i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; $\tau\tau'$ and $\tau'\tau$ fix every $x_i$, so they are the identity (uniqueness in the universal property) and $\tau$ is an automorphism with $\tau(x_i-a_i)=x_i$. Hence $\tau(\mathfrak m')=\mathfrak p_0:=(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ and $\tau$ induces a ring isomorphism $R:=P_{\mathfrak m'}\cong P_{\mathfrak p_0}$, $p/s\mapsto\tau(p)/\tau(s)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-origin-regular-local] (with $d=n$), $P_{\mathfrak p_0}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $n$ whose maximal ideal is generated by $x_1/1,\dots,x_n/1$; transporting by the isomorphism, $R$ is a regular local ring of dimension $n$ with maximal ideal $M=\mathfrak m'R$ generated by $(x_1-a_1)/1,\dots,(x_n-a_n)/1$, and residue field $R/M\cong P/\mathfrak m'=\kappa$ ($\mathfrak m'$ maximal). By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], $\dim_\kappa M/M^2=\dim R=n$; the $n$ classes of $(x_i-a_i)/1$ span $M/M^2$ (they generate $M$), hence form a $\kappa$-basis of $M/M^2$. Therefore the $\kappa$-linear map $\ell:\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\kappa\,\mathrm dx_i\to M/M^2$, $\mathrm dx_i\mapsto(x_i-a_i)/1\bmod M^2$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180): 'the right lower horizontal arrow induces an isomorphism (+) kappa(m') dx_i -> m'/(m')^2' (here read in the local ring R = k[x]_{m'}, where the source's 'regular local ring' k[x_1..x_n]_{m'} is used)

proof.text: (The diagram of the source: first order Taylor expansion.) Claim: for every $p\in P$, $p\equiv p(a)+\sum_{i=1}^n(\partial p/\partial x_i)(a)\,(x_i-a_i)\bmod\mathfrak m'^2$, with $\partial/\partial x_i$ as in [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] and $(-)(a)=\mathrm{ev}_a$ (step 3). The set of $p$ satisfying it is a $k$-subspace containing the constants and each $x_j$ ($x_j=a_j+(x_j-a_j)$, $\partial x_j/\partial x_i=\delta_{ij}$); it is closed under products: if $p\equiv p(a)+u$ and $q\equiv q(a)+v$ with $u=\sum_i(\partial p/\partial x_i)(a)(x_i-a_i)$, $v=\sum_i(\partial q/\partial x_i)(a)(x_i-a_i)$ in $\mathfrak m'$, then $pq\equiv p(a)q(a)+p(a)v+q(a)u\bmod\mathfrak m'^2$ (as $uv\in\mathfrak m'^2$), and by the Leibniz rule $(\partial(pq)/\partial x_i)(a)=p(a)(\partial q/\partial x_i)(a)+q(a)(\partial p/\partial x_i)(a)$, so the claim holds for $pq$; hence for all monomials and all of $P$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For $f\in I\subseteq\mathfrak m'$ we have $f(a)=0$, and $(\partial f/\partial x_i)(a)\in k$ has the same image in $\kappa=P/\mathfrak m'=S/\mathfrak m$ as $\partial f/\partial x_i$ (step 3), i.e. as $\alpha(\partial f/\partial x_i)$. Mapping the congruence into $M/M^2$ ($\mathfrak m'^2$ maps into $M^2$) gives, for $f\in I$: $f/1\bmod M^2=\ell(\bar\delta(f))$, where $\bar\delta(f)=\sum_i\overline{\alpha(\partial f/\partial x_i)}\,\mathrm dx_i\in\bigoplus_i\kappa\,\mathrm dx_i$ is the image of $\mathrm d(f\bmod I^2)$ under $\bigoplus_iS\,\mathrm dx_i\to\bigoplus_i\kappa\,\mathrm dx_i$. This is the commutativity of the diagram the source leaves to the reader.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180): the commutative diagram I -> I/I^2 -> (+) S dx_i -> m'/(m')^2, dx_i |-> x_i - a_i ('proof commutativity omitted')

proof.text: ($I/\mathfrak m'I$ injects into $\bigoplus\kappa\,\mathrm dx_i$.) Apply $-\otimes_S\kappa$, $\kappa=S/\mathfrak m$, to $\mathrm d$ and its left inverse $\lambda$ of step 2: $(\lambda\otimes1)\circ(\mathrm d\otimes1)=\mathrm{id}$, so $\mathrm d\otimes1:(I/I^2)\otimes_S\kappa\to\bigoplus_i\kappa\,\mathrm dx_i$ is injective. Since $S=P/I$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m'/I$, $(I/I^2)\otimes_S\kappa=I/(I^2+\mathfrak m'I)=I/\mathfrak m'I$ (as $I\subseteq\mathfrak m'$ gives $I^2\subseteq\mathfrak m'I$), and $\mathrm d\otimes1$ sends $f\bmod\mathfrak m'I$ to $\bar\delta(f)$ of step 5. Hence $\bar\delta$ induces an injective $\kappa$-linear map $I/\mathfrak m'I\to\bigoplus_i\kappa\,\mathrm dx_i$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180): 'Hence the corresponding map I/m'I -> (+) kappa(m') dx_i is injective'

proof.text: (Generators of $IR$ by Nakayama.) $I/\mathfrak m'I$ is a $\kappa$-vector space spanned by the classes of $g_1,\dots,g_m$ (step 2); let $c$ be its dimension and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in I$ elements whose classes form a basis. Let $IR\subseteq R$ be the ideal generated by the $f/1$, $f\in I$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; it is generated by $g_1/1,\dots,g_m/1$, so it is a finitely generated $R$-module. The map $I\to IR/M\cdot IR$, $f\mapsto f/1$, is $P$-linear, kills $\mathfrak m'I$ (as $\mathfrak m'R=M$), and is surjective: an element $\sum_jr_j(f_j'/1)$ of $IR$ ($r_j\in R$, $f'_j\in I$) has $r_j\equiv\lambda_j/1\bmod M$ for some $\lambda_j\in P$ ($R/M\cong P/\mathfrak m'$), so it is congruent to $(\sum_j\lambda_jf_j')/1$ mod $M\cdot IR$. So the classes of $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ span the $\kappa$-vector space $IR/M\cdot IR$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] (local ring $R$, finitely generated module $IR$) $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ generate the ideal $IR$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180): 'Say dim (I/m'I) = c and pick f_1..f_c in I which map to a basis of I/m'I. By Nakayama's Lemma 00DV (lemma-NAK) we see that f_1..f_c generate I_{m'} over k[x_1..x_n]_{m'}'

proof.text: ($f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ is a regular sequence in $R$.) By step 5, the class of $f_j/1$ in $M/M^2$ is $\ell(\bar\delta(f_j))$. The vectors $\bar\delta(f_1),\dots,\bar\delta(f_c)$ are linearly independent (images of a basis of $I/\mathfrak m'I$ under the injective map of step 6) and $\ell$ is an isomorphism (step 4), so the classes of $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ in $M/M^2$ are linearly independent; in particular $c\le n$. Extend them by $n-c$ of the basis vectors $(x_i-a_i)/1\bmod M^2$ (step 4) to a $\kappa$-basis of $M/M^2$ (exchange lemma), and let $h_1,\dots,h_n\in M$ be the corresponding elements, $h_j=f_j/1$ for $j\le c$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] (applied to the finitely generated $R$-module $M$) $h_1,\dots,h_n$ generate $M$; they are $n=\dim R$ elements of the regular local ring $R$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] $h_1,\dots,h_n$ is a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Then $h_1,\dots,h_c$ is a regular sequence: condition (1) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $i\le c$ is the same as for the whole sequence, and (2) holds since $(h_1,\dots,h_c)\subseteq M\neq R$. So $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$ is a regular sequence in $R$ generating $IR$ (step 7).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180): 'Hence our generators f_1..f_c of I_{m'} map to elements whose classes in m'/(m')^2 are linearly independent over kappa(m'). Therefore they form a regular sequence in the ring k[x_1..x_n]_{m'} by Lemma 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM)'

proof.text: (Condition (5) of 00SC at $\mathfrak m$.) By step 8 the ideal $IR=IP_{\mathfrak m'}$ of $R=P_{\mathfrak m'}$ is generated by the regular sequence $f_1/1,\dots,f_c/1$, where $\mathfrak m'$ is the inverse image in $P$ of the prime $\mathfrak m$ of $S=P/I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lci-regular-sequence-global-complete-intersection] (with $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m$, $e=c$, $h_j=f_j/1$) there is $g_{\mathfrak m}\in S$, $g_{\mathfrak m}\notin\mathfrak m$, such that $S_{g_{\mathfrak m}}$ is a global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180): 'This verifies condition (5) of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci) hence S_g is a global complete intersection over k for some g in S, g not in m'

proof.text: (Covering $\operatorname{Spec}S$.) Let $J$ be the set of maximal ideals of $S$ and, for $\mathfrak m\in J$, $g_{\mathfrak m}$ as in step 9. Every prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$ is contained in some maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ (a proper ideal lies in a maximal ideal), and $g_{\mathfrak m}\notin\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak q$ gives $\mathfrak q\in D(g_{\mathfrak m})$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; so $\operatorname{Spec}S=\bigcup_{\mathfrak m\in J}D(g_{\mathfrak m})$ (if $S=0$, both sides are empty and $J=\emptyset$). As $S$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra (step 2) and every $S_{g_{\mathfrak m}}$ is a global complete intersection over $k$, $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] (2).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00T5 (lemma-smooth-over-field, line 37180): 'As this works for any maximal ideal of S we conclude that S is a local complete intersection over k'
